name: DietPi
summary: Ultra-lightweight and highly optimised Linux distribution based on Debian GNU/Linux, designed for single-board computers (Raspberry Pi, ARM SBC) and x86-64 servers, integrating interactive administration tools and RAM logging.

content.introduction: DietPi is an ultra-lightweight and highly stripped-down Linux distribution derived from Debian GNU/Linux. Initially designed by Daniel Knight in 2015 and maintained by MichaIng, it aims to offer an execution base of maximum frugality for single-board computers (SBC) and compact servers, reducing RAM consumption at rest to a few tens of megabytes.
content.what_is_it: Technically, DietPi relies on a minimal Debian image (or Raspberry Pi OS on the foundation's hardware), stripped of all superfluous components, bulky documentation and non-critical resident services. The system installs less than half of the usual packages of a general-purpose distribution, while providing a suite of semi-graphical interactive utilities (TUI) developed in Bash to orchestrate the whole machine in a few keystrokes.
content.resource_optimization_and_ramlog: The major technical signature of DietPi lies in its architecture for reducing flash memory wear. Thanks to `dietpi-RAMlog`, all system event logs (`/var/log`) are redirected to a virtual disk in RAM (tmpfs). The logs are rewritten in grouped fashion on the microSD card or flash medium only once per hour or when the system shuts down. This mechanism considerably extends the lifetime of memory cards and relieves the I/O controller from continuous writes, guaranteeing increased responsiveness.
content.interactive_toolset_and_automation: DietPi is configured through dedicated interactive tools: `dietpi-config` makes it possible to finely adjust the hardware parameters (CPU frequency governors, safe overclocking profiles, audio, display, network and stress tests), `dietpi-drive_manager` handles partitioning and mounting of Samba/NFS shares, while `dietpi-backup` takes care of system backup and restoration. The initial installation can be fully automated and headless by filling in the declarative `dietpi.txt` file before the first boot.
content.software_catalog_and_ready_services: At the heart of the ecosystem lies `dietpi-software`, a deployment manager offering more than 100 optimised and preconfigured applications, ready to be installed in one click. This catalogue covers lightweight web servers (Nginx, Lighttpd), DNS ad blockers (Pi-hole, AdGuard Home), self-hosting and storage solutions (Nextcloud, Vaultwarden), multimedia servers (Plex, Jellyfin), container environments (Docker, Docker Compose) and lightweight graphical interfaces (XFCE, LXDE), without requiring complex manual configuration.
content.hardware_matrix_and_maintenance: Initially oriented towards the Raspberry Pi, DietPi offers optimised images for a huge variety of ARM architectures (Raspberry Pi 1 to 5, Odroid, Orange Pi, Pine64, NanoPi, ASUS Tinker Board) as well as for conventional x86-64 PCs and virtualisation hypervisors (VirtualBox, VMware, Proxmox VE, Hyper-V). Maintenance is carried out through transparent incremental updates via the `dietpi-update` utility, allowing the system to move from one major Debian version to the next without service interruption.
content.security_options_fail2ban_and_tls: DietPi documents its security options as software items installed through `dietpi-software` rather than as a hardened default profile. Fail2Ban is offered to protect the system from brute-force attacks by banning the source address: detection covers the OpenSSH and Dropbear servers, an address is banned after three failed SSH login attempts by default, and the ban lasts ten minutes, with the status of blocked addresses readable from the command line. The second item is transport encryption for the services a user exposes: Certbot, the official Let's Encrypt client, obtains and applies the certificate, and the `dietpi-letsencrypt` command walks through the domain, port and e-mail settings before applying them. The documentation notes that port 80 has to stay open and forwarded even when the site is served over HTTPS, because renewal uses it.
advantages: Extremely low hardware resource consumption (often less than 50 MB of RAM at rest).
Preservation of the lifetime of microSD cards thanks to the `dietpi-RAMlog` RAM logging system.
`dietpi-software` catalogue of more than 100 popular applications preconfigured and optimised for the target architectures.
Interactive configuration tools (`dietpi-config`) facilitating the adjustment of hardware, network and overclocking.
Very broad hardware support including almost all ARM SBC boards, x86-64 PCs and virtual machines.
Installation process fully automatable without screen or keyboard (headless) through the `dietpi.txt` file.
disadvantages: Deliberately stripped-down system requiring manual installation of additional base tools for users accustomed to complete distributions.
The administration interface relies on text-mode menus (TUI), without a native web graphical interface integrated by default.
Automated configuration scripts can conflict with non-standard manual customisations of the system files under `/etc/`.
Less oriented towards everyday general-purpose desktop workstation use than towards the role of network appliance or lightweight server.
Dependence on the upstream Debian repositories and on manufacturer kernel builds for certain exotic SBCs.
who_is_it_for: Owners of Raspberry Pi boards and ARM nano-computers looking for maximum performance and a minimal memory footprint.
Home server (homelab) users wishing to host microservices (Pi-hole, VPN servers, home automation) on modest hardware.
Owners of old PCs or x86-64 laptops wishing to recycle an ageing machine into a silent autonomous server.
System administrators deploying fleets of network probes or lightweight application nodes automatable through `dietpi.txt`.
who_is_it_not_for: Beginner users looking for a complete turnkey visual desktop system with office suite and multimedia player preinstalled.
Developers requiring a full set of compilation tools and libraries present from the first boot without configuration.
High-performance computing infrastructures requiring complex enterprise virtualisation environments or distributed Ceph clusters.
Commercial environments requiring contractual technical assistance guarantees with a service level agreement (SLA).
content.verdict: DietPi is a minimalist distribution derived from Debian, designed to minimise the hardware footprint on single-board computers (SBC) and x86-64 virtual machines. Thanks to the automation of system configuration, the preservation of flash storage through its RAM logging system (dietpi-RAMlog) and an interactive menu for installing ready-to-use applications (dietpi-software), it constitutes an efficient technical solution for home servers, self-hosting and lightweight network gateways.

components.name: Debian
components.note: Base system: DietPi presents itself as a highly optimised minimal Debian OS; the page does not state the Debian version.

components.name: DietPi-Software
components.note: Installs and optimises the selected software ready to run, through lightweight Whiptail menus, according to the project site.

components.name: DietPi-RAMlog
components.note: Logging option that keeps logs in RAM; the site presents it as the performance option, alongside rsyslog and logrotate for log-critical servers.

components.name: DietPi-Config
components.note: Configuration utility presented beside DietPi-Software among the project utilities; the page does not detail the available settings.

relations.name: Debian
relations.note: Linux distribution from which the entire system base and package manager of DietPi are directly derived.

relations.name: Raspberry Pi OS
relations.note: Official operating system for Raspberry Pi boards to which DietPi offers an ultra-lightweight and resource-efficient alternative.

relations.name: Alpine Linux
relations.note: Independent Linux distribution focused on extreme minimalism and a reduced memory footprint.

relations.name: OpenMediaVault
relations.note: Network storage solution whose automated installation is offered directly within the DietPi software catalogue.
